questions.q: Ravi lowers a stone into a glass filled to the brim with water, and some water spills over. What does this show?
questions.a: The stone takes up space that the water was using
o: The stone takes up space that the water was using
The stone has mass, so its weight squeezes water out
The stone is insoluble, so water cannot mix with it
The stone is hard, so water cannot enter it

questions.q: Kiran says: 'I poured a full 1.5 L jug of lassi into five tumblers of 250 mL and three cups of 125 mL, filled every one of them to the top, spilled nothing, and the jug is now empty.' Show that his account cannot be right.
questions.a: 1.5 L = 1500 mL of lassi was in the jug. The tumblers and cups together hold 5 x 250 mL + 3 x 125 mL = 1250 mL + 375 mL = 1625 mL. Filling all of them would need 1625 mL, 125 mL more than the 1500 mL there was, so with nothing spilled at least one cup could not have been filled to the top.
s: 1.5 L changed to 1500 mL
Total space in the tumblers and cups: 1625 mL
1625 mL is 125 mL more than 1500 mL, so not all could be filled

questions.q: True or False? A 500 mL bottle full of honey and a 500 mL bottle full of water hold the same volume of liquid, but they need not have the same mass. Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: True. 500 mL tells the volume, the space each liquid occupies, so the volumes are equal. Mass is a different property: different materials filling the same space can be heavier or lighter. Only weighing both bottles on a balance shows how their masses compare.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: equal volume, but mass is a different property, found by weighing

questions.q:
Three identical paper cups are half-filled: A with water, B with sand, C with pebbles. On a balance the cups read A 110 g, B 160 g and C 145 g. An empty cup reads 10 g.
(a) Arrange the cups from heaviest to lightest.
(b) Find the mass of the contents alone in each cup.
(c) Do the contents of the three cups occupy about the same space? Give a reason.
(d) What do (b) and (c) together show about mass and volume?
(e) Use the definition of matter to show that the contents of all three cups, and the cups themselves, are matter.
questions.a: (a) B, C, A. (b) A: 110 - 10 = 100 g; B: 160 - 10 = 150 g; C: 145 - 10 = 135 g. (c) Yes: each identical cup is filled half-way, so the contents fill about the same space (the same volume). (d) Materials that occupy about the same volume can have different masses; having the same volume does not mean having the same mass. (e) Water, sand, pebbles and the paper cups each occupy space and have mass, as the balance readings show, so all of them are matter.
s: Part (a): B, C, A
Part (c): same space, as each identical cup is half-filled
Part (d): same volume does not mean same mass
Part (e): all occupy space and have mass, so all are matter

questions.q:
A 1 kg bag of cotton and a 1 kg bag of iron nails are placed on the two pans of a balance.
(a) Which pan goes down? Explain.
(b) Which bag takes up more space, and what does this show about mass and volume?
questions.a: (a) Neither: both bags have the same mass, 1 kg, so the balance stays level. (b) The cotton bag takes up far more space. Equal masses do not mean equal volumes; mass (the quantity of matter) and volume (the space it occupies) are different properties.
s: Part (a): neither, equal mass of 1 kg
Part (b): cotton takes more space; same mass does not mean same volume

questions.q:
For a sports day in Cuttack, a school canteen will serve buttermilk in cups of 250 mL. To find how much its containers hold, the cook fills each with water and pours it into 250 mL cups until the container is empty.
Container | Full cups poured | Water left over after the last full cup
Tall steel can | 6 | none
Wide clay pot | 9 | none
Plastic jug | 4 | 150 mL
(a) Find the volume of each container in mL.
(b) The cook says, 'The tall can holds the most, because it is the tallest.' Accept or reject his claim, using (a).
(c) Work backwards: 45 students will each get one cup. How many litres of buttermilk are needed, and how many wide clay pots must be filled to hold exactly that much?
questions.a: (a) Tall can: 6 x 250 mL = 1500 mL. Clay pot: 9 x 250 mL = 2250 mL. Jug: 4 x 250 mL + 150 mL = 1150 mL. (b) Reject. The clay pot holds 2250 mL, more than the can's 1500 mL. Volume is the space a container can hold, which height alone does not show. (c) 45 x 250 mL = 11250 mL = 11.25 L; 11250 mL / 2250 mL = 5 clay pots.
s: Part (a): 1500 mL, 2250 mL and 1150 mL
Part (b): rejected, since the pot holds 2250 mL against 1500 mL; height is not volume
Part (c): 11.25 L and 5 clay pots

questions.q: A jug holds 1.8 L of buttermilk. It is poured into tumblers of 250 mL, one after another, until no more full tumblers can be filled. The buttermilk left in the jug is ___ mL.

Statement 1: A stone and the air inside a balloon are both matter.
Statement 2: Mass and volume are two properties possessed by all materials.
Statement 3: Since every material is matter, every material is also lustrous, hard and soluble in water.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: Statements 1 and 2 only
o: Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statement 2 only
All three statements

questions.q: Priya pours water from a jug holding 1.2 L into an empty 1 L bottle, and some water is left in the jug. Given 1 L = 1000 mL, how much water is left in the jug, and why could she not pour it all in?
questions.a: 1200 mL - 1000 mL = 200 mL is left. The water in the jug had a volume of 1200 mL, more space than the bottle can offer (1000 mL), so it could not all fit.
s: 200 mL left, worked from 1200 mL and 1000 mL
Reason: the water's volume was greater than the space in the bottle

questions.q:
A shop in Pune sells mustard oil in packs of 1 L at Rs 180, 500 mL at Rs 95 and 200 mL at Rs 40. Use 1 L = 1000 mL.
(a) Write the volume of each pack in mL.
(b) Find the cost of 1 L of oil bought as 500 mL packs, and as 200 mL packs.
(c) Which pack gives the cheapest litre?
(d) A family needs exactly 2.4 L for the month, bought in whole packs. Find the cheapest combination and its cost.
(e) The shop now adds a 2 L pack at Rs 350. Does this change the cheapest way to buy exactly 2.4 L? Show the new cost.
questions.a: (a) 1000 mL, 500 mL and 200 mL. (b) Two 500 mL packs: 2 x Rs 95 = Rs 190; five 200 mL packs: 5 x Rs 40 = Rs 200. (c) The 1 L pack, at Rs 180 a litre. (d) 2.4 L = 2400 mL = 2 x 1000 mL + 2 x 200 mL, costing 2 x Rs 180 + 2 x Rs 40 = Rs 440 (other exact combinations cost Rs 450 or more). (e) Yes: 2400 mL = 2000 mL + 2 x 200 mL, costing Rs 350 + 2 x Rs 40 = Rs 430, Rs 10 less than Rs 440 (no other exact combination is cheaper).
s: Part (a): 1000 mL, 500 mL, 200 mL
Part (b): Rs 190 and Rs 200
Part (c): the 1 L pack
Part (d): two 1 L and two 200 mL packs, Rs 440
Part (e): one 2 L and two 200 mL packs, Rs 430, cheaper than Rs 440

questions.q: A building's underground tank holds 2 m³ of water when full and is now one-quarter full. Given 1 m³ = 1000 L, how many buckets of 20 L each are needed to fill it to the top?
Meena says: 'Three 400 mL bottles hold more milk than a 1 L carton, but less milk than five 250 mL packs.' Check her claim, showing the working.
questions.a: Yes, she is right. 1 L = 1000 mL. Three 400 mL bottles hold 3 x 400 mL = 1200 mL, which is more than 1000 mL. Five 250 mL packs hold 5 x 250 mL = 1250 mL, which is more than 1200 mL. So 1000 mL < 1200 mL < 1250 mL.
s: Verdict: yes, the claim is correct
1 L = 1000 mL and 3 x 400 mL = 1200 mL, more than the carton
5 x 250 mL = 1250 mL, more than 1200 mL

questions.q:
(a) A student writes the mass of a pencil as 5 kg and the volume of water in a full bucket as 15 mL. Explain why each value is not sensible.
(b) Rewrite both with a sensible unit.
questions.a: (a) 5 kg is about the mass of a big bag of rice, far too heavy for a pencil; 15 mL is only about a spoonful or two, far too little for a full bucket. (b) 5 g and 15 L.
s: Part (a): both values judged against real sizes
Part (b): 5 g and 15 L

questions.q:
Every value in Column II has the number 5; only the unit differs. Match each quantity (Column I) with its sensible value (Column II).
Column I
1. Water in a school's full overhead tank
2. Water in a small bucket
3. A bag of atta for a family
4. A new pencil
Column II
a. 5 kg
b. 5 L
c. 5 m³
d. 5 g

A school in Chennai has an overhead tank of 5 m³, filled every morning by a water tanker. Its 400 students each use about 10 L of water in a school day. On about 10 days a year the tanker comes only after school is over, and the school pays Rs 800 for an emergency tanker each time. The school could add a second tank, filled along with the first every morning: 2 m³ for Rs 12,000 or 5 m³ for Rs 30,000. Use 1 m³ = 1000 L.
(a) How many litres does the full tank hold, and how many do the students use in a day?
(b) How much water is left at the end of a day, and how many litres short is the school on a day the morning tanker does not come?
(c) Which second tank, if either, would end the emergency trips? Decide, using (b) and the costs.
questions.a: (a) 5 x 1000 = 5000 L held; 400 x 10 = 4000 L used. (b) 5000 - 4000 = 1000 L left, so on a late day the school is 4000 - 1000 = 3000 L short. (c) With the 2 m³ tank, 7000 L are stored and 3000 L are left at the end of a day, still 1000 L short of a day's 4000 L, so the emergency trips continue. With the 5 m³ tank, 10,000 L are stored and 6000 L are left, enough for a late day. The 5 m³ tank ends the trips; it costs Rs 30,000 against 10 x Rs 800 = Rs 8,000 a year, so it pays for itself in 30,000 / 8,000 = 3.75 years.
s: Part (a): 5000 L and 4000 L
Part (b): 1000 L left, 3000 L short
Part (c): the 2 m³ tank still leaves 1000 L short; the 5 m³ tank covers a late day and pays back in 3.75 years

questions.q: A family buys 2 kg 500 g of rice, 750 g of dal and 1 kg 250 g of sugar. Given 1 kg = 1000 g, find the total mass in grams and in kilograms, and write both answers correctly with their units.
questions.a: Rice 2500 g + dal 750 g + sugar 1250 g = 4500 g. In kilograms: 4500 / 1000 = 4.5 kg. Written as 4500 g and 4.5 kg (space between number and unit, lower case, no 's').
s: Each item changed to grams: 2500 g, 750 g, 1250 g
Total: 4500 g
4.5 kg, both written correctly

questions.q: A grocer writes five shelf labels: 'Atta 5 kgs', 'Oil 1 L', 'Milk 500 ml', 'Rice 10 kg', 'Water tank 2m³'. How many of the labels break a rule for writing units?

A bottle of juice holds 2 L 250 mL. Given 1 L = 1000 mL:
(a) Write the volume in mL, using the correct way of writing the unit.
(b) How many cups of 150 mL each can be filled from it?
questions.a: (a) 2000 mL + 250 mL = 2250 mL (written with a space between number and unit, lower-case m and capital L). (b) 2250 / 150 = 15 cups.
s: Part (a): 2250 mL, correctly written
Part (b): 15 cups
